intent.raw_query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March 2026

selected_hotel.name: Djemaa el-Fna, Medina, Marrakech Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Explore Djemaa el-Fna Square
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the beating heart of Marrakech at this UNESCO-listed square. Watch snake charmers, storytellers, acrobats, and musicians perform as the sun sets. Sample street food like harira soup, msemen flatbread, and freshly squeezed orange juice from the surrounding stalls.

experiences.name: Camel Trek and Overnight Sahara Camp
experiences.description: Ride a camel into the golden dunes of Erg Chebbi near Merzouga for a breathtaking sunset. Spend the night in a traditional Berber desert camp under a sky full of stars, enjoy live Gnawa music around the campfire, and wake up for a spectacular sunrise over the dunes.

experiences.name: Guided Tour of the Medina and Souks
experiences.description: Navigate the labyrinthine medieval alleyways of Marrakech's ancient Medina with a local guide. Discover the Medersa Ben Youssef, the historic Koutoubia Mosque, and the vibrant souks selling spices, leather goods, lanterns, and handwoven carpets. Learn about centuries of Moroccan craftsmanship and trade.

experiences.name: Visit the Bahia Palace and Saadian Tombs
experiences.description: Step back into Morocco's royal past by touring the stunning 19th-century Bahia Palace with its intricate zellige tilework, carved cedar ceilings, and lush gardens. Then visit the nearby Saadian Tombs, a beautifully preserved 16th-century royal necropolis rediscovered in 1917.

experiences.name: Moroccan Cooking Class in a Riad
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class hosted inside a traditional riad in the Medina. Visit the local spice market with your host, then learn to prepare classic Moroccan dishes such as chicken tagine with preserved lemon, couscous with seven vegetables, and bastilla. Enjoy your creations over mint tea.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara)
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Djemaa el-Fna, Medina, Marrakech Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Take Bus No. 19 or a shared grand taxi from the airport to the Medina (budget tip: bus costs ~4 MAD vs. 70–100 MAD for a private taxi). Check in to your riad/boutique stay near Djemaa el-Fna and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: First immersion into Djemaa el-Fna Square — the beating heart of Marrakech. Wander the square and watch snake charmers, street musicians, and henna artists (look but don't engage unless you're happy to pay). Stroll into the adjacent Souk Semmarine to get your bearings in the labyrinthine medina. Free to explore.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Djemaa el-Fna as the square transforms at sunset — food stalls open and the atmosphere becomes electric. Choose a numbered food stall for a budget dinner (stalls 1–100 are all similar; avoid aggressive touts). Enjoy harira soup, merguez sausages, and fresh-squeezed orange juice.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a coffee and msemen (Moroccan flatbread) at a local café near the riad for ~10 MAD
meals.lunch: Grab a snack on arrival — try a sandwich or bowl of harira from a street stall near the medina for ~15–25 MAD
meals.dinner: Djemaa el-Fna food stalls: harira soup (~5 MAD), brochettes (~20 MAD), fresh orange juice (~4 MAD) — full meal for ~50–70 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day — keep it light. Exchange currency at a bank or ATM in the medina (avoid airport exchange booths for poor rates). Budget ~150 MAD for the day including transport and meals. March weather in Marrakech is mild (15–22°C), perfect for walking.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Koutoubia Mosque gardens at sunrise (non-Muslims cannot enter the mosque but the gardens and exterior are free and stunning). Then head to the Saadian Tombs (entrance ~70 MAD) — a 16th-century royal necropolis rediscovered in 1917, one of Marrakech's most impressive historical sites. Arrive early (opens 9:00) to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Bahia Palace (entrance ~70 MAD) — a stunning 19th-century palace with intricate Moroccan tilework, carved cedarwood ceilings, and lush courtyards. Afterward, wander the mellah (Jewish quarter) nearby — free to explore, historically rich. Visit the El Badi Palace ruins (entrance ~70 MAD) for panoramic views and ancient grandeur.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to the medina souks for an evening shopping stroll — practice your bargaining skills at the spice souk and leather goods stalls. Settle in at a rooftop café overlooking Djemaa el-Fna for mint tea and people-watching as the square lights up.

meals.breakfast: Café de France or any local café on Djemaa el-Fna — café au lait and msemen or beghrir (Moroccan pancakes) for ~20–30 MAD
meals.lunch: Cheap local restaurant in the medina — try a tagine set menu (tagine + bread + mint tea) for ~50–70 MAD at a restaurant away from the main square
meals.dinner: Restaurant Chez Bahia near the Bahia Palace area — couscous or kefta tagine for ~60–80 MAD, popular with locals

day_by_day.notes: Combined entrance to Saadian Tombs + Bahia Palace + El Badi Palace costs ~210 MAD. Budget day total (meals + entries): ~350–400 MAD. Wear comfortable shoes — lots of walking on uneven medina stones. Dress modestly when visiting religious/royal sites.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Ourika Valley and Atlas Mountains (approx. 60 km from Marrakech). Take a shared grand taxi from Bab er Rob near Djemaa el-Fna (~30–40 MAD each way). Hike up to the Setti Fatma waterfalls — a series of 7 cascades through Berber villages. The first waterfall is an easy 20-minute walk; the upper ones require a guided scramble (local guides offer their services for ~50–100 MAD tip).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Berber village of Setti Fatma, visit local argan oil cooperatives (free to enter, no obligation to buy), and enjoy the lush green valley scenery — a dramatic contrast to the city. Head back to Marrakech by shared taxi in the mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relax and recover at your riad. Visit the free Cyber Park (Arsat Moulay Abdeslam) near the medina for a peaceful evening stroll. Enjoy dinner in the medina at a local eatery.

meals.breakfast: Eat at your riad if breakfast is included, or grab amlou (almond-argan spread) on bread at a local bakery for ~15 MAD
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local Berber restaurant in Setti Fatma overlooking the river — tagine and salad for ~60–80 MAD (check prices before sitting down)
meals.dinner: Medina local restaurant — try pastilla (sweet-savoury pigeon pie) or a lamb tagine for ~60–80 MAD

day_by_day.notes: Total day cost (transport + lunch + guide tip): ~250–300 MAD. Start early (8:00–9:00) to make the most of the valley. Wear sturdy shoes for the waterfall hike. Bring water and sunscreen. March can still be cool in the Atlas Mountains — bring a light layer.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech early (6:00–7:00) via a budget shared minibus or CTM/Supratours bus toward Merzouga and the Sahara Desert (approximately 9–10 hours, ~150–200 MAD one way). The route passes through the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m), the kasbahs of Ouarzazate, the Draa Valley, and the Todra Gorge area. Enjoy the scenery from the window — this journey is an attraction in itself.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in the Merzouga / Erg Chebbi area in the late afternoon. Check in to a budget desert camp or guesthouse (~150–250 MAD per night for a shared dorm or basic private room). Drop your bags and prepare for the desert experience. The towering orange dunes of Erg Chebbi (up to 150m high) come into view — take in the breathtaking landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Join a budget camel trek into the dunes at sunset (typically included with desert camps or available for ~100–150 MAD). Ride to a traditional Berber camp in the dunes, watch the sunset over the Sahara, and enjoy a bonfire with traditional music (guembri and drums) under a sky exploding with stars — one of Morocco's most magical experiences.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departure in Marrakech — grab msemen and coffee at a medina café for ~20 MAD
meals.lunch: Stop for a quick lunch at a roadside restaurant in Ouarzazate or along the route — harira, bread, and a tagine for ~50–70 MAD
meals.dinner: Dinner at the desert camp — typically included with camp stay (traditional Moroccan meal: tagine, couscous, bread, mint tea)

day_by_day.notes: Book your desert transport in advance — CTM bus or a shared minibus via a budget agency. Total transport + camp cost: ~350–450 MAD. Bring a warm layer — desert nights in March drop to 5–10°C. Bring a headlamp, sunscreen, and a scarf/shemagh for dust. This is the longest travel day of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (5:30–6:00) to watch the Sahara dawn from the dunes — an unmissable, otherworldly experience as the light shifts from deep purple to gold across the sand. Take a sunrise walk or short camel ride back to the camp. After breakfast, explore the base of the Erg Chebbi dunes on foot — try sandboarding (boards available to rent at camp for ~30–50 MAD).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the small village of Merzouga on foot or by bicycle (rentable for ~50 MAD/day). Explore the local market, visit a fossil and mineral shop (the region is famous for trilobite fossils), and meet local Gnawa musicians. Optional: visit the salt lake (Dayet Srji) nearby — a seasonal flamingo habitat in spring. Free to explore.
day_by_day.evening: Spend a final quiet evening at the desert camp or guesthouse. Stargaze from the dunes — with zero light pollution, the Milky Way is fully visible. Optional: arrange a second night in the dunes or prepare for the return journey.

meals.breakfast: Included at desert camp — typically Moroccan bread, jam, amlou, coffee, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Local café or guesthouse in Merzouga village — omelette, bread, and tea for ~30–40 MAD
meals.dinner: Guesthouse or camp dinner — tagine and couscous for ~60–80 MAD if not included in accommodation

day_by_day.notes: Sandboarding is a fun, low-cost adventure activity. Budget day total: ~200–300 MAD. Stay hydrated — desert air is very dry. If you want to push further, a day trip to Todra Gorge (80 km away) is possible by shared taxi (~60 MAD each way) — dramatic 300m-high canyon walls.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Merzouga early and begin the return journey to Marrakech via a different route through the Draa Valley and Ait Benhaddou (a UNESCO World Heritage ksar/fortified village used as a filming location for Game of Thrones, Gladiator, and Lawrence of Arabia). Arrive at Ait Benhaddou by midday (shared transport or budget agency minibus, ~100–150 MAD).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Ait Benhaddou ksar (entrance ~10 MAD, guide optional ~50–100 MAD). Climb to the top of the ksar for panoramic views of the surrounding desert landscape. Cross the shallow river on stepping stones to reach the village. Browse local artisan shops for affordable souvenirs — silver jewelry, pottery, and leather goods.
day_by_day.evening: Continue the journey back to Marrakech (2.5–3 hours from Ait Benhaddou via Ouarzazate). Arrive in Marrakech by early evening. Return to your riad, freshen up, and enjoy a final evening in the medina — revisit Djemaa el-Fna for dinner and entertainment.

meals.breakfast: At desert camp or guesthouse before departure — included or ~30 MAD
meals.lunch: Lunch near Ait Benhaddou — local auberge tagine meal for ~60–80 MAD
meals.dinner: Djemaa el-Fna food stalls — a final feast of Moroccan street food: harira, brochettes, snail soup (optional!), and fresh juice for ~60–80 MAD

day_by_day.notes: This is a long travel day (~8–9 hours total including stops). The Ait Benhaddou stop breaks the journey perfectly. Total transport for the day: ~250–350 MAD. March light is beautiful for photography at Ait Benhaddou in the afternoon. Confirm your return transport the night before in Merzouga.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — visit the Majorelle Garden (entrance ~150 MAD, includes the Berber Museum). The vivid cobalt-blue villa and exotic plant collection are iconic. Alternatively, for a completely free option, explore the peaceful Menara Gardens (free entry) with its olive groves and reflecting pool backed by Atlas Mountain views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping in the medina souks — best buys on a budget include: argan oil products, Moroccan spices (cumin, ras el hanout, saffron), leather slippers (babouches), hand-painted ceramic bowls, and woven rugs. Practice hard bargaining — start at 30–40% of the asking price. Visit the Mellah spice market for the best prices on spices.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the airport for departure (allow 2 hours before flight). Take Bus No. 19 back to the airport (~4 MAD) or a pre-negotiated grand taxi (~80–100 MAD). Enjoy one last mint tea at the airport — a fitting farewell to Morocco.

meals.breakfast: Final Moroccan breakfast at a medina café — café au lait, fresh-squeezed orange juice, msemen with honey and argan oil for ~30–40 MAD
meals.lunch: Budget lunch at Café Clock (Marrakech branch near the Kasbah) — camel burger or Moroccan wrap for ~60–80 MAD, a beloved local institution
meals.dinner: Light snack at the airport or early dinner in the medina before departure — allow time for transport

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden is pricier but worth it for garden and museum lovers. Free alternative: Menara Gardens. Budget the full day at ~300–400 MAD including garden entry, last meals, and airport transport. Keep small bills (10–20 MAD notes) for tips and small purchases. Tipping culture: 10–20 MAD for guides, porters, and helpful locals is appreciated.

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara) Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Djemaa el-Fna, Medina, Marrakech Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to your boutique riad in the Medina near Djemaa el-Fna (approx. 20–30 min by taxi, ~80–100 MAD). Check in, freshen up, and settle into your accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk around Djemaa el-Fna square and its immediate surroundings. Explore the outer edges of the souks near Rue des Épices, visit a small spice stall, and soak in the atmosphere without pressure. Pop into the Musée de la Place (small entry fee ~10 MAD) for a quick historical overview of the square.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to Djemaa el-Fna as the sun sets — the square transforms into a massive open-air spectacle with storytellers, musicians, snake charmers, and food stalls. Stroll and watch before settling in for dinner at one of the terrace restaurants overlooking the square.

meals.breakfast: Skipped / light snack on the plane
meals.lunch: Café de France or Café Argana terrace — mint tea, msemen (Moroccan flatbread), and a fresh orange juice (~40–60 MAD)
meals.dinner: Djemaa el-Fna food stalls (stall #1 or #14 are popular) — harira soup, grilled merguez, and kefta brochettes (~80–120 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the afternoon arrival. Keep luggage minimal for the taxi. Exchange some cash at the airport or a medina bureau de change (better rates). Wear comfortable walking shoes — medina streets are uneven cobblestone.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the stunning Bahia Palace (entry ~70 MAD) — a 19th-century vizier's palace with ornate Moorish architecture, painted ceilings, and tranquil courtyards. Then walk 10 minutes to El Badi Palace ruins (entry ~70 MAD), a 16th-century Saadian palace that once rivaled Versailles. Climb the ramparts for panoramic medina views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Saadian Tombs (entry ~70 MAD) — a hidden necropolis of the Saadian dynasty with beautifully decorated mausoleums. Afterward, wander through the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) nearby, visiting the Lazama Synagogue (free/donation) and the vibrant spice and goldsmith market streets.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the riad to rest, then head out to the Mouassine neighborhood — a quieter, more artisan-focused part of the medina. Browse leather goods, ceramics, and lanterns in the evening souks. End the evening at a rooftop restaurant for a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: At your riad (typically included) — Moroccan spread of msemen, amlou (argan oil dip), honey, fresh fruit, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Chez Bahia near the palace district — tagine of chicken with preserved lemon and olives, fresh bread (~80–100 MAD)
meals.dinner: Nomad Restaurant (Mouassine area) — modern Moroccan cuisine, lamb pastilla or vegetable tagine (~150–200 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Start early (9:00 AM) to beat crowds at Bahia Palace. The Saadian Tombs are small and can get crowded by midday — aim to visit before 11:30 AM or after 3:00 PM. Carry water and sunscreen as March afternoons can be warm (~20–24°C).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Majorelle Garden (entry ~150 MAD) — a breathtaking botanical garden with cobalt-blue buildings, exotic cacti, and lily ponds, originally designed by painter Jacques Majorelle and later restored by Yves Saint Laurent. Combine with the adjacent Berber Museum (included in ticket) showcasing Amazigh jewelry, textiles, and artifacts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Medina's heart — the main souks. Explore the labyrinthine passages of Souk Semmarine, Souk des Teinturiers (dyers' souk), and Souk Cherratin (leather). Visit a traditional tannery for an overhead view of the dyeing pits (free with a guide tip). Try your hand at negotiating for a small souvenir — a leather pouch, ceramic bowl, or argan oil product.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a traditional Gnawa music performance — ask your riad host for a local venue or check Café Clock Marrakech for live music events. Alternatively, enjoy a hammam experience at a mid-range hammam (Hammam El Bacha or a riad-recommended local hammam, ~150–250 MAD for scrub and steam).

meals.breakfast: At your riad
meals.lunch: Café Kif Kif near Majorelle — fresh salads, Moroccan wraps, and smoothies (~80–120 MAD)
meals.dinner: Le Jardin restaurant (Mouassine) — set in a beautiful courtyard garden, serves Moroccan-Mediterranean fusion (~180–220 MAD per person)

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden opens at 8:00 AM — go early to avoid tour groups. Photography is allowed in the garden but not inside the museum. In the souks, a rough rule: the first price quoted is 2–3x the fair value. Be friendly but firm when bargaining. Hammam visits are best booked in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech early (6:00–7:00 AM) by private shared transfer or organized day-tour heading toward the Sahara via the Draa Valley and Ouarzazate — this is a full travel day toward the desert. Drive through the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m) in the High Atlas, stopping for photos at scenic viewpoints and a brief tea stop in a Berber village.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Ouarzazate (~4 hours from Marrakech). Visit the Kasbah Taourirt (entry ~20 MAD) — a UNESCO-listed mudbrick fortress and one of Morocco's best-preserved kasbahs. Walk through the narrow alleys and meet local artisans. Continue driving toward the Draa Valley, passing through palm groves, ksour (fortified villages), and dramatic desert landscapes. Arrive at your desert camp near Zagora or continue to Merzouga (if using a 2-day transfer).
day_by_day.evening: If staying near Zagora: settle into a mid-range desert camp (traditional Berber tent with basic amenities), enjoy a short camel ride at sunset into the dunes (~30–45 min, included in most camp packages), and watch the stars emerge over the Sahara — one of Morocco's most magical experiences.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at your riad before departure
meals.lunch: Roadside Berber restaurant near Tizi n'Tichka or Ouarzazate — harira, kefta tagine, fresh bread (~60–90 MAD)
meals.dinner: At the desert camp — traditional Berber dinner around a campfire: vegetable tagine, couscous, Moroccan salads, and mint tea (~included in camp package or ~150–200 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: This is a long travel day (~8–10 hours total driving). Book a shared transfer or small group tour in advance from Marrakech (typically ~400–600 MAD per person for shared, or ~1,200–1,500 MAD for private). For Merzouga (the grand Erg Chebbi dunes), an overnight stay requires departing even earlier or splitting over 2 days. Zagora offers a closer, quieter desert experience. Bring a warm layer — desert nights in March drop to 5–10°C.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (around 6:00 AM) to witness the Sahara dawn — colors shift from deep purple to gold over the dunes. Take a morning walk or short camel trek to a high dune for panoramic views. If at Merzouga/Erg Chebbi, consider a quad bike ride across the dunes (organized through camp, ~200–300 MAD for 1 hour) for an adventure thrill.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nearby Berber village with your camp guide to learn about desert life, traditional mud-brick architecture, and nomadic culture. Stop at a fossil market (the region is famous for trilobite and ammonite fossils) — great for unique, affordable souvenirs. Begin the return journey toward Marrakech, stopping at the Todra Gorge (if routing via Tinghir) — dramatic 300m-high canyon walls perfect for a short walk.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight stop in a mid-range guesthouse in Boumalne Dades or Ouarzazate, or continue driving back to Marrakech if using a faster route (arriving late evening). Freshen up and enjoy a quiet dinner after two days of desert adventure.

meals.breakfast: At the desert camp — Moroccan breakfast of bread, jam, honey, eggs, and mint tea (included)
meals.lunch: Café/restaurant near Todra Gorge or Dades Valley — mixed Moroccan salads, tagine, fresh orange juice (~80–100 MAD)
meals.dinner: Guesthouse dinner in Boumalne Dades or Ouarzazate — couscous with seven vegetables, Berber omelette, mint tea (~100–150 MAD)

day_by_day.notes: Sunrise in the Sahara is unmissable — set your alarm. Sand can be cold and windy in the early morning, so layer up. If quad biking, closed shoes are essential. The Todra Gorge detour adds ~1.5 hours but is highly recommended for dramatic scenery. Confirm your return transport arrangements the night before.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Marrakech (arriving mid-morning if you stayed in Ouarzazate, or late morning if driving from further). Check back into your riad and freshen up. Use the late morning to visit the Ben Youssef Madrasa (entry ~70 MAD) — a stunning 14th-century Islamic school with intricate zellige tilework, carved cedar wood, and stucco plasterwork; one of Morocco's finest examples of Moorish architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Musée de Marrakech (entry ~50 MAD) housed in a 19th-century palace — rotating exhibitions of Moroccan art, photography, and artifacts. Then visit the nearby Koubba Ba'adiyn (entry ~20 MAD), the city's only surviving Almoravid-era structure (12th century). Spend the late afternoon in the quieter northern medina neighborhoods, browsing artisan workshops and smaller, less touristy souks.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself to a special farewell-to-the-desert dinner at a mid-range traditional restaurant. Consider a cooking class experience if available through your riad (typically 300–400 MAD, often includes dinner) — learn to make tagine, bastilla, or Moroccan pastries.

meals.breakfast: On the road — roadside café coffee and msemen, or light snack from a bakery (~20–30 MAD)
meals.lunch: Earth Café Marrakech (vegetarian-friendly, near Ben Youssef) — fresh salads, lentil soup, Moroccan wraps (~80–120 MAD)
meals.dinner: Dar Yacout or Riad des Mille et Une Nuits — atmospheric riad restaurant with traditional Moroccan feast: pastilla, multiple tagines, couscous, dessert (~250–350 MAD per person, mid-range splurge)

day_by_day.notes: Ben Youssef Madrasa is one of Marrakech's most photogenic spots — visit before 10:00 AM or after 3:00 PM for fewer crowds. If the cooking class appeals, book it through your riad 1–2 days in advance. This day is intentionally slower-paced to recover from desert travel.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — visit the Mellah Sunday market (or the Rahba Kedima spice square) for last-minute shopping: argan oil, ras el hanout spice blends, dried rose petals, saffron, and handmade crafts. Then take a peaceful walk along the medina ramparts (the ancient red-ochre walls) for a final atmospheric stroll. Visit the Koutoubia Mosque gardens (non-Muslims cannot enter the mosque, but the gardens and exterior are beautiful and free).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time — if evening flight, enjoy a leisurely lunch and a final mint tea at a rooftop café overlooking the medina. Pack, check out of the riad, and store luggage with reception if needed. Transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport (allow 45–60 minutes before departure, including transfer time).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Marrakech. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final riad breakfast — savor the Moroccan spread one last time
meals.lunch: Café des Épices (Rahba Kedima) — rooftop terrace with medina views, fresh juices, salads, and sandwiches (~80–100 MAD)
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight (if departing in the evening)

day_by_day.notes: Marrakech airport can be busy on Sundays — arrive at least 2.5 hours before international departure. Keep some MAD for last-minute tips, porter fees, or a final coffee. Argan oil and saffron purchased from medina shops are genuine and significantly cheaper than airport prices — buy before you leave the medina. Taxis to the airport cost ~80–100 MAD (negotiate beforehand or use a metered petit taxi).

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Morocco (Marrakech and Sahara) Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Djemaa el-Fna, Medina, Marrakech Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from airport to boutique riad in Djemaa el-Fna Medina. Check-in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome mint tea ceremony hosted by riad staff.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk through Djemaa el-Fna square as it awakens in the late afternoon. Explore the immediate surroundings — watch storytellers, snake charmers, and street performers from the terrace of a rooftop café. Visit the nearby Koutoubia Mosque gardens for a peaceful stroll and iconic photo opportunity.
day_by_day.evening: Immerse in the full spectacle of Djemaa el-Fna at dusk when the square transforms into a vibrant open-air theatre. Wander among food stalls, musicians, and acrobats before retiring for a curated private dinner at the riad.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (mid-day arrival)
meals.lunch: Light welcome spread at the riad upon check-in — Moroccan pastries, fresh juices, seasonal fruits, and mint tea prepared by in-house staff
meals.dinner: Private rooftop dinner at the riad featuring traditional Moroccan tasting menu: harira soup, bastilla au pigeon, slow-cooked lamb tagine with preserved lemon and olives, orange blossom crème brûlée — paired with Moroccan rosé wine

day_by_day.notes: Arrival day is intentionally relaxed to allow for jet lag recovery and acclimatization. Confirm private airport transfer in advance. Riad check-in is typically from 14:00 — luggage storage available if needed upon early arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Saadian Tombs (opening at 09:00) — a 16th-century royal necropolis with stunning Andalusian-Moorish architecture. Follow with a visit to El Badi Palace ruins, where a knowledgeable historian guide explains the grandeur of the Saadian dynasty. Includes exclusive early-access arrangement to avoid crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the atmospheric souks of the Medina with a dedicated cultural guide — navigate the dyers' souk (Souk Sabbaghin), the spice market, and the leather tanneries. Visit a prestigious argan oil cooperative for a private demonstration and tasting. Stop at a master craftsman's atelier for a hands-on introduction to Moroccan zellige tilework.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on a rooftop terrace overlooking Djemaa el-Fna and the Koutoubia minaret. Followed by a premium dinner at one of Marrakech's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Full Moroccan breakfast at the riad: msemen flatbreads, amlou (almond-argan spread), fresh-squeezed orange juice, soft-boiled eggs with cumin, honey, and Moroccan coffee
meals.lunch: Private lunch at a traditional dar (heritage home) in the Medina — a curated spread of Moroccan salads, kefta brochettes, vegetable couscous, and fresh fruit
meals.dinner: Dinner at Dar Yacout or equivalent luxury restaurant — a legendary Marrakchi experience in a 1001 Nights setting with live Gnawa music, multiple-course Moroccan feast including pigeon pastilla, mechoui lamb, and honey-drenched chebakia pastries

day_by_day.notes: Book Saadian Tombs early-access and Dar Yacout reservation well in advance. Dress modestly when visiting religious and heritage sites. The souk tour is best done before 13:00 to avoid afternoon heat in March.

day_by_day.morning: Private visit to the Bahia Palace — one of Morocco's most ornate 19th-century palaces. Exclusive guided tour of its 160 rooms, lush gardens, and intricate painted ceilings. Follow with a visit to the Maison de la Photographie for a curated look at historic Moroccan photography and cultural heritage.
day_by_day.afternoon: Immersive cooking class at a premium culinary school in the Medina — learn to prepare traditional Moroccan dishes including tagine, couscous, and pastilla under the guidance of a master chef. Class includes a market visit to select fresh ingredients from the souks.
day_by_day.evening: Hammam and spa experience at a luxury riad or five-star spa — traditional black soap scrub (kessa), ghassoul clay mask, and full-body argan oil massage. A deeply restorative Moroccan wellness ritual.

meals.breakfast: Riad breakfast with a special addition of freshly baked meloui crepes with honey and goat cheese, alongside a Moroccan herbal tea selection
meals.lunch: The dishes prepared during the cooking class are enjoyed as a communal lunch with the chef and fellow participants in a beautifully set traditional dining room
meals.dinner: Intimate dinner at Le Jardin or equivalent garden restaurant in the Medina — contemporary Moroccan cuisine in a lush courtyard setting: roasted vegetable briouats, chermoula sea bass, saffron-scented chicken with preserved lemon, rose water panna cotta

day_by_day.notes: The hammam session should be booked for early evening (18:00–20:00) to allow the cooking class to finish comfortably. Bring a change of comfortable clothing for the hammam. The cooking class typically runs 3–4 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech by private luxury 4x4 vehicle at 07:00 for the journey toward the Sahara Desert via the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m altitude). Stop at a Berber village in the High Atlas Mountains for tea with a local family and panoramic mountain views. Continue through the rose valley of Dadès.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the Drâa Valley and Ouarzazate — the 'Door of the Desert.' Visit the UNESCO-listed Aït Benhaddou ksar (fortified village), a breathtaking 11th-century earthen citadel used as a filming location for Lawrence of Arabia, Game of Thrones, and Gladiator. Private guided tour with a local historian.
day_by_day.evening: Continue to Merzouga / Erg Chebbi dunes. Arrive at a luxury desert camp or boutique desert lodge before sunset. Mount camels for a guided sunset camel trek into the Sahara dunes — watch the sky turn gold and crimson over the sea of sand.

meals.breakfast: Early packed gourmet breakfast prepared by the riad — artisan sandwiches, fresh fruit, pastries, and thermos coffee/tea for the road
meals.lunch: Traditional Berber lunch at a family-run auberge in the Drâa Valley — slow-cooked lamb tagine with prunes and almonds, Moroccan salads, fresh bread, and mint tea
meals.dinner: Candlelit Berber dinner under a billion stars in the Sahara — a lavish spread of mezze, grilled meats, couscous royale, and Moroccan sweets accompanied by live Gnawa drumming and music around a bonfire

day_by_day.notes: This is the longest travel day (~8–10 hours total with stops). Depart early to maximize daylight at Aït Benhaddou. Wear layers — the High Atlas can be cold in March mornings. Pack a small overnight bag for the desert camp; main luggage can remain in the vehicle.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before dawn for a private sunrise hike to the top of the Erg Chebbi dunes (up to 150m high) — one of the most awe-inspiring experiences in North Africa. Watch the Sahara light up in shades of amber and rose. Return to camp for a leisurely breakfast. Optional: sandboarding on the dunes or a guided 4x4 desert excursion to fossil sites and nomadic encampments.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a nomadic Berber family in the desert for an authentic cultural exchange — learn about traditional desert life, try hand-ground coffee, and see how they navigate the landscape. Explore the Merzouga village and its small museum of Saharan geology and fossils. Relax at the luxury camp's pool or spa in the afternoon heat.
day_by_day.evening: Second evening in the Sahara — private stargazing session with a telescope guided by a local astronomer. The Sahara's zero light pollution makes it one of the world's premier stargazing locations. Enjoy a private dinner set up on a dune top for two or a small group.

meals.breakfast: Sumptuous camp breakfast after sunrise: Saharan-style flatbread, honey, dates, fresh fruit, eggs cooked to order, Berber coffee and fresh-squeezed juice
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the desert lodge — mezze platters, grilled vegetable skewers, watermelon, and chilled Moroccan mint lemonade
meals.dinner: Exclusive private dune-top dinner experience — white-tablecloth setup in the desert with a curated 4-course menu including harira, mechoui slow-roasted lamb, saffron couscous, and almond-stuffed dates with argan honey drizzle

day_by_day.notes: Sunrise is approximately 07:15 in mid-March — set alarm for 05:30 to hike up in time. Bring a warm layer for the early morning; temperatures can drop to 5–10°C at night in the desert in March. Sunscreen and a headscarf are essential during the day.

day_by_day.morning: Depart the Sahara after breakfast and begin the scenic return journey to Marrakech via the Todgha Gorge — a spectacular canyon with 300-metre-high rock walls carved by the Todgha River. Private guided walk through the gorge with a local geologist. Visit a traditional Berber carpet cooperative in the Dadès Valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Valley of Roses (Vallée des Roses) — particularly stunning in March as the damask roses begin to bloom. Stop at a rose water distillery for a private tour and tasting. Arrive back in Marrakech by late afternoon. Check back into the riad and refresh.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell evening in Marrakech — visit the Mellah (historic Jewish quarter) and the vibrant Place des Ferblantiers for a final evening stroll. Enjoy a premium cocktail experience at a rooftop bar before the farewell dinner.

meals.breakfast: Final desert camp breakfast — dates, Berber bread, argan honey, yogurt, eggs, and Saharan herbal tea
meals.lunch: Picnic-style gourmet lunch prepared by the camp and enjoyed at the Todgha Gorge — artisan cheeses, cured meats, Moroccan flatbreads, olives, and fresh fruit in a spectacular natural setting
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a top-tier Marrakech restaurant such as Nomad Rooftop or La Maison Arabe — contemporary Moroccan-Mediterranean fusion cuisine: saffron-cured salmon, lamb rack with ras el hanout crust, dark chocolate fondant with orange blossom ice cream, paired with curated Moroccan wines

day_by_day.notes: The return drive from Merzouga to Marrakech is approximately 7–8 hours with stops — depart by 07:30 to arrive comfortably before dinner. The Valley of Roses is best visited in late March to early April; early March may see early blooms. Confirm riad reservation is held for return.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — visit the serene Majorelle Garden, the iconic cobalt-blue botanical garden originally designed by French painter Jacques Majorelle and later restored by Yves Saint Laurent. Includes the Berber Museum within the garden. Arrive at opening time (09:00) for a peaceful experience before crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute luxury shopping in the Medina — visit a premier Moroccan artisan gallery for handcrafted leather goods, bespoke jewellery, fine carpets, and argan cosmetics. Stop at a renowned pâtisserie for a selection of Moroccan sweets and pastries to take home. Return to the riad for final packing and check-out.
day_by_day.evening: Private luxury transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport. Enjoy the Moroccan airport lounge experience before departure. Reflect on an extraordinary week of culture, history, desert adventure, and premium hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Celebratory final breakfast at the riad — the full spread: msemen, beghrir (honeycomb pancakes), amlou, fresh orange juice, Moroccan coffee, honey, and seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: Leisurely lunch at Café du Livre or a garden restaurant near Majorelle — light mezze, Moroccan-style salad niçoise, fresh seafood pastilla, and chilled rose wine
meals.dinner: Farewell airport lounge dining or a final quick dinner at a premium café near the Medina before the transfer — Moroccan lamb kefta wrap, fresh juices, and a box of handmade Moroccan chocolates and sweets for the journey home

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden tickets should be purchased online in advance to guarantee entry — it is one of Marrakech's most visited sites. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for airport transfer and check-in. Tip riad staff generously — a standard premium gratuity is 200–300 MAD per staff member for a week-long stay.
